name: NGC 1939 (Hubble)
blurb: NGC 1939, an old globular cluster in the Large Magellanic Cloud, seen by Hubble.
label: ngc1939-hubble
story: An ancient, metal-poor globular cluster of the Large Magellanic Cloud, roughly as old as the oldest globular clusters of our own galaxy. A much younger cluster, NGC 1938, lies along the same line of sight but is unlikely to be physically associated with it.

claims.text: NGC 1939 is an old LMC globular cluster
NGC 1939 is coeval with the oldest Galactic and LMC globular clusters
The NGC 1939 field contains another, much younger cluster, NGC 1938, unlikely to be physically associated
LMC stands for the Large Magellanic Cloud
